title: Sweep a table clear while another robot arm picks blocks off it
instruction: Pick up the hand broom and sweep everything off the table while the other arm picks out the red blocks. Don't touch the other arm or the block it's holding.
context: Two robots sharing a bench have to work at the same time, not take turns. The other arm won't wait or steer around you, so you have to time your strokes around it.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot. Positions are the centre of each object, measured from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, then sideways toward the controlled arm (negative means toward the other arm). A hand broom, 80 g, stands on its bristles at (22, 36) cm, its length running front to back: a 20 x 5 x 2 cm blue plastic back over a 20 x 4 x 2.5 cm block of black bristles, and an 8 cm rubber grip (2 cm across, 3 cm deep) held on two posts over the back's middle, rising 30 degrees toward the front, its middle 9.2 cm above the table. A grey plastic bin, 15 x 15 cm inside with 6 cm walls 1 cm thick, at (16, -34) cm. Four red painted wooden cubes, 4 cm, 40 g, at (20, 8), (32, 8), (40, 0) and (15, 2) cm. Clutter: two yellow rubber balls, 4 cm, 30 g, at (15, 21) and (36, 20) cm; a white crumpled paper ball, about 4.5 cm, 10 g, at (18, 27) cm; two green empty plastic boxes, 6 x 4 x 3 cm, 20 g, lying flat with their long side front to back, at (26, 24) and (44, 12) cm; a blue painted wooden cube, 3 cm, 20 g, at (42, 34) cm. The other arm waits 2 s, then takes the red blocks to its bin in the order listed, side by side, about one every 6 s, and finishes over the bin at about 26 s. A block that is no longer on the table is skipped. It does the same in every trial.
scoring: Items swept off the table divided by items counted: the 6 clutter items, plus each red block that ends up off the table. Red blocks the other arm puts in its bin, or that stay on the table, don't count either way. 0 if the controlled arm or the broom ever touches the other arm or the block in its hand; the run stops at the first touch.
run_limit: 600 steps (30 seconds at 20 Hz), about when the other arm drops its last block, so waiting it out earns nothing.
reset_notes: Stand the broom back where it started (the demo does this itself), empty the bin, and put back everything that went onto the floor.
fidelity: Approximate. The bristles are one solid block, and every item is rigid. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real ones, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm is scripted on the true scene state.
